newsitem.title: UK: Coffee crop estimates - Main S AMERICAN producers.
newsitem.headline: Coffee crop estimates - Main S AMERICAN producers.

text.p: The following table gives latest estimates of 1996/97 coffee crops in main South American coffee producing countries (estimates of 1995/96 crops in brackets).
Crop years and approximate main harvesting periods (as supplied by economists) follow each entry (in million 60 kg bags) -
SEE BELOW TABLE FOR MORE DETAILED NOTES ON HARVESTS, CRUCIAL WEATHER PERIODS.
BRAZIL's coffee crop is harvested from end-April to end-September. Frost is a mainly a danger during June-August.

Drought also hit the crop in July 1994. Rains are crucial by mid-September to help flowerings. Trees normally have three flowerings, one of which will account for 60 percent of the crop. They can occur to mid-December if severely delayed.
November and December are peak months for cherry setting and rains are necessary throughout this period to help in setting.
Rains are then important for the size of the coffee bean until the start of the harvest).

COLOMBIA has a "mitaca" crop which begins at the end of March and a later and bigger crop, which begins in September. Heavy rains in the rainy season in December-February can adversely affect flowering and formation of cherries.

PERU's harvest begins in the eastern lowlands in early March, moves up the slopes of the Andes through the the year and ends in November in the higher altitudes. Plants flower in the lowlands in September and this ends in the highlands in December. Plants are most susceptible to high winds, drought and torrential rains between flowering and harvest.
